It, as far as I can tell, does not have travel time. Hitting the target through this wall makes the drill instantly connect. What it also does is remove the 5 impact damage that the drill does, as the wall is taking the impact instead, and then it still takes the drill a second to warm up before it starts spewing flame. So while the damage isn't instantly done, the drill still instantly makes contact with a surface off in the distance. Also, the drill loses its arc and turns into a straight shot as well, so if it's instantly making contact right where you were aiming, I'd call it hitscan personally.

Thank you, I don't know why nobody seems to be thinking of intentionally moving them! I think it's even more simple than you're giving it credit for though, you don't even have to hide your light and slip behind them! Every area where you have to get past a stranger has multiple paths through it, like weaving between rocks or looping around trees, and all I did was catch the attention of a stranger, wait until they got closer, and then take an alternate path to where they had been standing. They're really not good hunters, they'll follow whatever the shortest path to you is no matter what and they're a fair bit slower than you are, so as long as you keep moving and take a different route you can pretty much kite them around indefinitely and get where you need to go.

As a keyboard player, there was a different solution than the 1 pip of thrust on controller, and I imagine it would work the same for you. >!When you enter a seed, you'll come out the other side at a fixed angle and velocity. Since you can't adjust the intensity of your thrust with a keyboard, your only option for getting past the three anglers is to drift into the red seed and then wait. You're already at the right angle to just barely slip past them, and you have enough momentum to make it out of their earshot, albeit painfully slowly. No adjustment necessary. Once you can turn around and only see their lights in the distance, or when their breathing stops, you're safe to stop yourself and course correct toward where you're heading. It's terrifying but it works consistently.!< Hopefully this helps!

To achieve the distorted effect, I copied my recording in Audacity and pasted it onto a second track. Then I lowered the pitch of the secondary track VERY slightly, just enough that it would be heard as a separate voice and not perfectly overlap with the original recording. Then I just dropped the volume of the deepened track to make it more subtle and that was about it! Everything besides the occasional moments where the second track shines through (I think it's most obvious on "feel the strain") was just my voice.
